_comment: Route contract — the CONTENT pin for the two hand-maintained route lists.
route-contract.test.ts asserts lib/redirects.ts and lib/navigation.ts are
EXACTLY equal to this file, in both directions: a route cannot be added,
removed, retargeted or silently swapped without a deliberate edit here.
This file is INDEPENDENT on purpose — it is never generated from the source
it pins. Keep it that way: a generated pin verifies nothing.
Editing it = declaring intent. When a route change is intentional, update
this file in the same commit and say why in the commit message.
navRoutes order is sidebar display order, so it is order-sensitive.
knownShadowed: pages that exist on disk AND are also a redirect source,
so the 307 fires before routing and they can NEVER be reached. Discovered
by this test on 2026-10-21 — pre-existing debt, not introduced by it.
Cleared 2026-10-24: all 36 were deleted (page.tsx 109 -> 73). MAY ONLY
SHRINK from here: deleting a dead page means removing its entry in the
same commit. Adding one is a new unreachable page.
knownWorkspaceNamespace: routes nested under a CONCEPT prefix. Ruling
(2026-10-21): 'workspace is a philosophy, not a page' — a URL namespace
is an address space (load-bearing: redirects, bookmarks, scopes, tests),
while a concept is a taxonomy. A taxonomy must not own an address space,
because when the concept changes the URLs cannot follow.
Workspace is a SCOPE, not a location: you are IN one, everything else is
scoped by it. It belongs in a selector + a nav grouping LABEL, not a path
prefix. MAY ONLY SHRINK — adding an entry here is a new concept-namespaced
route, which is what this ruling forbids.
